items.stem: Distinguish between 'political executive' and 'permanent executive'.

items.markingKey: (d) 'coalition government' means a government formed by an alliance of two or more parties when no single party has a majority.
options: A system in which the President is both head of state and head of government and is elected separately
The principle that the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha
The organ of government that implements laws and policies
A government formed by an alliance of two or more parties when no single party has a majority

items.stem: The following statement about the executive and its types is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "India has a presidential system like the USA."
items.answer: India has a parliamentary system.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (India has a parliamentary system.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the permanent executive: bureaucracy is correct?
items.answer: All India Service officers are recruited by the Union but work in the states.
items.markingKey: (b) The others are wrong: They are recruited through competitive examinations. It is permanent and continues when governments change. They are recruited by the Union through the UPSC.
options: Civil servants are elected by the people.
All India Service officers are recruited by the Union but work in the states.
The bureaucracy changes whenever the government changes.
All India Service officers are recruited by the state governments.

items.stem: "India chose the parliamentary system." Examine this statement with reference to the executive and its types.
items.answer: The statement is valid. The makers wanted an executive accountable to the elected representatives and familiar from colonial experience.
items.markingKey: 3 marks: 1 for accepting or qualifying the statement, 1 for the reason (the makers wanted an executive accountable to the elected representatives and familiar from colonial experience.), 1 for supporting evidence from the chapter.

items.stem: The following statement about the President of India is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and justify your correction: "The President of India is elected directly by the people."
items.answer: The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement (The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college.); 1 mark for a supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Distinguish between 'collective responsibility' and 'coalition government'.
items.answer: Collective responsibility: the principle that the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. Coalition government: a government formed by an alliance of two or more parties when no single party has a majority.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 for explaining 'collective responsibility' (the principle that the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.) and 1 for 'coalition government' (a government formed by an alliance of two or more parties when no single party has a majority.), with the contrast made clear.

items.stem:
Answer the following with reference to the President of India.
(a) Give a reason for the following: The President is elected indirectly. (2)
(b) The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give one supporting fact: "The President of India is elected directly by the people." (2)
items.answer: (a) The makers wanted a ceremonial head who would not compete with the Prime Minister as a rival centre of power. (b) The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (a) 2 for the reason – the makers wanted a ceremonial head who would not compete with the Prime Minister as a rival centre of power. (b) 2 for the corrected statement – The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college. Credit a relevant supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: What is meant by 'bureaucracy' in the context of the permanent executive: bureaucracy?
items.answer: The body of trained, permanent civil servants who carry out the policies of the government.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: bureaucracy correctly explained as the body of trained, permanent civil servants who carry out the policies of the government.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers is NOT correct?
items.answer: A person must already be a Member of Parliament to be appointed a minister.
items.markingKey: (b) It is incorrect. A non-member can be appointed but must become a member within six months.
options: A person who is not a member of Parliament can become a minister but must become a member within six months.
A person must already be a Member of Parliament to be appointed a minister.
The Prime Minister allocates portfolios to ministers and coordinates the work of the government.
The Council of Ministers works on the principle of collective responsibility to the Lok Sabha.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the President of India and answer the questions that follow.
"The President can keep a bill pending without any time limit, which is called the pocket veto. The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college through the single transferable vote. When no party has a clear majority, the President uses discretion in appointing the Prime Minister."
(i) Which amendment made it binding on the President to act on the advice of the Council of Ministers? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'electoral college' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The President has some discretionary powers. (2)
items.answer: (i) The 42nd Amendment of 1976 (ii) The body of elected members of Parliament and the state legislative assemblies that elects the President. (iii) The Constitution allows the President to send back advice once, use the pocket veto and choose the Prime Minister when no party has a majority.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) The 42nd Amendment of 1976 (ii) The body of elected members of Parliament and the state legislative assemblies that elects the President. (iii) The Constitution allows the President to send back advice once, use the pocket veto and choose the Prime Minister when no party has a majority.

items.stem:
Answer the following with reference to the executive and its types.
(a) Give a reason for the following: India chose the parliamentary system. (2)
(b) The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give one supporting fact: "India has a presidential system like the USA." (2)
items.answer: (a) The makers wanted an executive accountable to the elected representatives and familiar from colonial experience. (b) India has a parliamentary system.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (a) 2 for the reason – the makers wanted an executive accountable to the elected representatives and familiar from colonial experience. (b) 2 for the corrected statement – India has a parliamentary system. Credit a relevant supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the President of India is NOT correct?
items.answer: The term of the President is six years.
items.markingKey: (a) It is incorrect. The President's term is five years.
options: The term of the President is six years.
The President is the nominal head of the executive and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
When no party has a clear majority, the President uses discretion in appointing the Prime Minister.
The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college through the single transferable vote.

items.stem:
Answer the following with reference to the permanent executive: bureaucracy.
(a) Give a reason for the following: The bureaucracy is called the permanent executive. (2)
(b) The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give one supporting fact: "All India Service officers are recruited by the state governments." (2)
items.answer: (a) Civil servants remain in service when governments change, giving continuity to administration. (b) They are recruited by the Union through the UPSC.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (a) 2 for the reason – civil servants remain in service when governments change, giving continuity to administration. (b) 2 for the corrected statement – They are recruited by the Union through the UPSC. Credit a relevant supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"India adopted the parliamentary system to make the executive accountable to the representatives of the people. In a semi-presidential system, the President and the Prime Minister share executive powers. The executive is responsible for implementing the laws made by the legislature. The political executive changes with elections, but the permanent executive continues."
(i) Explain the term 'executive', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: The makers of the Constitution did not want a strong single executive. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "Civil servants form the political executive." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) The organ of government that implements laws and policies. (ii) They feared concentration of power in one person. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: They form the permanent executive; ministers form the political executive.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) The organ of government that implements laws and policies. (ii) They feared concentration of power in one person. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: They form the permanent executive; ministers form the political executive.

items.stem:
Consider the following statements about the permanent executive: bureaucracy:
I. The bureaucracy is often criticised as insensitive to the needs of ordinary citizens.
II. The bureaucracy is expected to be politically neutral and serve any elected government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.
options: I only
II only
Both I and II
Neither I nor II

items.stem:
Answer the following with reference to the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.
(a) Give a reason for the following: The 91st Amendment limited the size of the Council of Ministers. (2)
(b) The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give one supporting fact: "A person must already be a Member of Parliament to be appointed a minister." (2)
items.answer: (a) Very large ministries had been formed to reward supporters and defectors. (b) A non-member can be appointed but must become a member within six months.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (a) 2 for the reason – very large ministries had been formed to reward supporters and defectors. (b) 2 for the corrected statement – A non-member can be appointed but must become a member within six months. Credit a relevant supporting fact from the NCERT chapter.

items.stem: The President can be removed from office through:
items.answer: impeachment for violation of the Constitution
items.markingKey: (a) impeachment for violation of the Constitution.
options: impeachment for violation of the Constitution
a Supreme Court order alone
a referendum
a decision of the Prime Minister

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the executive and its types and answer the questions that follow.
"The political executive changes with elections, but the permanent executive continues. In a parliamentary system, the executive is responsible to the legislature. In a presidential system, the President is both the head of state and the head of government."
(i) Which country has a presidential system of government? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'political executive' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: The permanent executive gives continuity to administration. (2)
items.answer: (i) The United States (ii) The elected leaders, such as the Prime Minister and ministers, who are responsible for government policy. (iii) Civil servants remain in office when governments change.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) The United States (ii) The elected leaders, such as the Prime Minister and ministers, who are responsible for government policy. (iii) Civil servants remain in office when governments change.

items.stem: Give a reason for the following: The Prime Minister is the most powerful person in the government.
items.answer: As leader of the majority he or she heads the Council of Ministers and controls policy.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: As leader of the majority he or she heads the Council of Ministers and controls policy. (1 mark for the reason, 1 for linking it to the statement).

items.stem:
Statement: The 91st Amendment limited the size of the Council of Ministers.
Which one of the following best explains this statement?
items.answer: Very large ministries had been formed to reward supporters and defectors.
items.markingKey: (c) Very large ministries had been formed to reward supporters and defectors.
options: The Prime Minister has to consult and accommodate coalition partners.
As leader of the majority he or she heads the Council of Ministers and controls policy.
Very large ministries had been formed to reward supporters and defectors.
Officers recruited by the Union serve in the states and can be disciplined only by the central government.
